record.title: Conjecture on the computed Wilf and enumeration classes of one-relator operads
record.statement: For $n=8,9,10,11,12$, let $A(n)$ be the number of Wilf classes and let $E(n)$ be the number of enumeration classes of one-relator binary operads with a relation of degree $n$. The computations provide upper bounds for these numbers, as listed in the paper's table. **Computed-class conjecture.** The values of $A(n)$ and $E(n)$ for $n=8,9,10,11,12$ are equal to the corresponding upper bounds listed in the table. The conjecture would establish the preceding Wilf-class conjecture for all $n\leq 12$; the claimed values are supported by stabilization of truncated generating functions, but are not proved in the source.

record.title: Dowling–Wilson top-heavy conjecture for subspace numbers
record.statement:
Let $E=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$ be a spanning subset of a $d$-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $w_i(E)$ denote the number of $i$-dimensional subspaces spanned by subsets of $E$. **Dowling–Wilson top-heavy conjecture.** For every $i<d/2$, one has

$$
w_i(E)\leq w_{d-i}(E).
$$

This conjecture, proposed by Dowling and Wilson in 1974, is a special case of a more general conjecture for matroids. The statement is known in some low-dimensional cases, including $w_1(E)\leq w_2(E)$ when $d=3$, but its general status is not established here.

record.title: Vertex decomposability of higher independence complexes of trees
record.statement: Let $T$ be a tree and let $r\geq 1$. The complex $\operatorname{Ind}_r(T)$ is the $r$-independence complex of $T$. **Tree higher-independence conjecture.** For any tree $T$ and $r\geq 1$, the complex $\operatorname{Ind}_r(T)$ is vertex decomposable. The conjecture extends the established result for caterpillar graphs. Computations verify vertex decomposability for all non-caterpillar trees with at most 10 vertices, but the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Fred M. Abdelmalek, Priyavrat Deshpande, Shuchita Goyal, Amit Roy and Anurag Singh, “Chordal graphs, higher independence and vertex decomposable complexes”, arXiv:2106.10863 (2023).

record.title: Atkin–Serre lower-bound conjecture for Ramanujan's tau function
record.statement:
Let $\tau(p)$ denote the Ramanujan tau function evaluated at a prime $p$.

**Atkin–Serre conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist constants $c(\varepsilon),d(\varepsilon)>0$ such that, for all primes $p>d(\varepsilon)$,

$$
|\tau(p)|\ge c(\varepsilon)p^{\frac{9}{2}-\varepsilon}.
$$

The source presents this as a stronger statement that would be needed to prove $|\tau(n)|\ge 100$ for $n>2$. It does not give a resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Kaya Lakein and Anne Larsen, “Some Remarks on Small Values of τ(n)”, arXiv:2107.03556 (2021).

record.title: Radenković–Gutman conjecture on the Laplacian energy of trees
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges, and Laplacian eigenvalues $\mu_1,\mu_2,\dots,\mu_{n-1},\mu_n=0$. Its **Laplacian energy** is

$$
LE(G)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\mu_i-\overline{d}|,
$$

where $\overline{d}=\frac{2m}{n}$ is the average degree. Let $T$ be a tree on $n$ vertices, and let $P_n$ and $S_n$ denote the path and star graphs on $n$ vertices, respectively. **Radenković–Gutman conjecture.**

$$
LE(P_n)\leq LE(T)\leq LE(S_n).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the path minimizes and the star maximizes Laplacian energy among all trees of order $n$. The source describes this extremal problem as open and reports that Radenković and Gutman formulated the conjecture after computing the relevant quantities for all trees up to $14$ vertices.
record.source_name: Hilal A. Ganiea, Bilal A. Rather and S. Pirzada, “On a conjecture of Laplacian energy of trees”, arXiv:2107.09162 (2021).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09162

record.title: The bounded Syracuse falling-time conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{syr}$ be the Syracuse map on odd positive integers, and let $\operatorname{sft}(n)$ denote the Syracuse falling time of an odd integer $n\geq 3$, namely the least positive number of Syracuse iterations needed to reach a value below $n$. **Bounded Syracuse falling-time conjecture.** There exists $C\geq 10$ such that

$$
\operatorname{sft}(n)\leq C
$$

for all $n\equiv 3\pmod 4$.

This conjecture seeks a uniform bound for Syracuse falling times on the residue class $3\pmod 4$. Computations establish bounds for a large finite range and for the known glide records, while the asserted global bound remains open.
record.source_name: Shalom Eliahou, Jean Fromentin and Rénald Simonetto, “Is the Syracuse falling time bounded by 12?”, arXiv:2107.11160 (2021).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.11160

record.title: The Syracuse falling-time conjecture for Mersenne-type integers
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{sft}(n)$ denote the Syracuse falling time of an odd positive integer $n$. **Mersenne Syracuse falling-time conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{sft}(2^{\ell}-1)=2
$$

for all $\ell\geq 4625$.

The assertion agrees with computations through $\ell=500000$, following a finite-range pattern in which the Syracuse falling time equals $2$ for all tested exponents from $4625$ onward. Its validity for all larger exponents is open.
record.source_name: Shalom Eliahou, Jean Fromentin and Rénald Simonetto, “Is the Syracuse falling time bounded by 12?”, arXiv:2107.11160 (2021).

record.title: The large-number falling-time conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{ft}(n)$ denote the falling time associated with the accelerated $3x+1$ map. **Large-number falling-time conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ft}(n)\leq 4
$$

for all $n\geq 2^{500}$.

This is a strong quantitative form of the Collatz conjecture, motivated by computations and heuristics suggesting that large integers rarely have falling time at least $5$. The threshold is supported by extensive finite searches, but the universal assertion remains open.

record.title: The large-number Syracuse falling-time conjecture
record.statement:

$$
\operatorname{sft}(n)\leq 2
$$

for all odd $n\geq 2^{5000}$.

This conjecture is the Syracuse analogue of the large-number falling-time bound and is motivated by computational evidence and heuristics for very large odd integers. Its truth beyond the tested finite range is open.

record.title: Schlage-Puchta's classification conjecture for triangular billiards
record.statement:
Let $1\leq s,t\leq n$ be integers such that $(n,s,t)=1$. Assume that for all $a$ with $(a,n)=1$ one has

$$
\frac{n}{2}<as\bmod n+at\bmod n<\frac{3n}{2}.
$$

**Schlage-Puchta's classification conjecture.** Then at least one of the following holds: $n\leq 78$, $s+t=n$, $s+2t=n$, $2s+t=n$, or $n$ is even and $|s-t|=\frac{n}{2}$. This classification concerns the arithmetic condition arising in the study of rational-angled triangular billiards with the lattice property; the supplied text does not establish whether the assertion is open or resolved.
record.source_name: Jan-Christoph Schlage-Puchta, “Addendum to "On triangular Billard"”, arXiv:2107.14025 (2021).

record.title: Poljak–Turzík's sticky matroid conjecture
record.statement:
We assume all matroids are finite. A matroid $M$ is **sticky** if, for every two matroids $M_1$ and $M_2$ with

$$
M=M_1|_{E(M)}=M_2|_{E(M)},
$$

there is a matroid $\widetilde{M}$ such that

$$
M_1=\widetilde{M}|_{E(M_1)}\quad\text{and}\quad M_2=\widetilde{M}|_{E(M_2)},
$$

where $E(N)$ denotes the ground set of $N$.

**Sticky matroid conjecture.** Stickiness of a matroid implies modularity. Thus, stickiness is equivalent to modularity.

Poljak and Turzík showed in 1982 that every modular matroid is sticky, so the conjecture asserts the converse. The supplied source does not state whether this converse has been resolved.
record.source_name: Jaeho Shin, “The Sticky Matroid Conjecture”, arXiv:2108.04757 (2021).

record.title: Conjecture on the row sum polynomials of the production matrix of an almost Riordan array
record.statement:
Let $P_n(x)$ denote the row sum polynomials of the matrix generated by regarding $\overline{A}$ as a production matrix. The initial polynomials are

$$
1,\quad 2-x,\quad x^2-3x+3,\quad -x^3+5x^2-8x+5,\quad x^4-8x^3+22x^2-25x+11,\ldots.
$$

**Row sum polynomial conjecture.** For every $n\geq 0$,

$$
P_n(x)=1+(1-x)\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(1-x)_i.
$$

Here $(1-x)_i$ denotes the falling factorial $(1-x)(-x)\cdots(2-x-i)$, with the empty sum interpreted as $0$ when $n=0$. This conjecture gives a closed formula for the row sums of the production matrix and extends the observed initial values; its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.

record.title: The curvature realization conjecture for the 24-cell Apollonian packing
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{R}^4}$ be the polytopal sphere packing obtained by rescaling a $1$-CBP projection of the $24$-cell by a factor of $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, and let $\Omega(\mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{R}^4})$ denote its associated packing. Write $\mathbb N$ for the set of natural numbers.

**Curvature realization conjecture.** The set of curvatures of $\Omega(\mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{R}^4})$ is $\mathbb N$.

Numerical experiments in the source suggest that every integer occurs without any modulo restriction. The statement is presented as one of two conjectures and remains open.
record.source_name: Iván Rasskin, “Regular polytopes, sphere packings and Apollonian sections”, arXiv:2109.00655 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.00655

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2021). “Nowadays, this conjecture is still open .”

record.title: The consecutive-curvature sequence conjecture for the 24-cell Apollonian packing
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{R}^4}$ be the polytopal sphere packing obtained by rescaling a $1$-CBP projection of the $24$-cell by a factor of $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, and let $\Omega(\mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{R}^4})$ denote its associated packing. A sequence of spheres is **consecutive tangent** if each sphere is tangent to the next one.

**Consecutive-curvature sequence conjecture.** There is a sequence of consecutive tangent spheres

$$
(b_0,b_1,\ldots)\subset \Omega(\mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{R}^4})
$$

such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, the curvature of $b_n$ is $n$.

This is a stronger, structured version of the preceding claim: it requires all natural-number curvatures to occur along one tangent sequence. The source presents it as an open conjecture motivated by numerical experiments.

record.title: The automorphism-group order conjecture for the graph R
record.statement:
Let $q=p^e$ be an odd prime power, and let $R$ be the graph under discussion with automorphism group $Aut(R)$. **Automorphism-group order conjecture.** For all odd prime powers $q$,

$$
|Aut(R)|=eq.
$$

The preceding discussion establishes a subgroup of this order and reports computational verification for all odd prime powers $q\leq 41$; the equality is presented as a conjecture for all odd prime powers.

record.title: Iwaniec's $L^p$ norm conjecture for the Ahlfors–Beurling operator
record.statement:
Let $T$ be the Ahlfors–Beurling operator on $L^p(\mathbb C)$, let $p^*=\max\{p,p/(p-1)\}$, and write $\|T\|_p$ for its operator norm. **Iwaniec's conjecture.** For every $p\in(1,\infty)$,

$$
\|T\|_p=p^*-1.
$$

The text describes this as an open problem originating with Iwaniec in 1982; it would imply optimal Sobolev integrability for quasiconformal maps and has further consequences in the calculus of variations.

record.title: The SP Goldbach conjecture
record.statement:
Let an **SP number** be a number of the form $pa^2$, where $p$ is prime and $a$ is a positive integer. A natural number is **sufficiently large** if it exceeds some fixed threshold.

**SP Goldbach conjecture.** Every sufficiently large natural number, whether even or odd, can be written as a sum of two SP numbers.

This is an analogue of the Goldbach conjecture without an even–odd parity restriction. The claim was verified computationally beyond $10^9$ and is reported to hold for all numbers starting at $3931$, but remains unproved.

record.title: Turán inequality conjecture for the plane-partition polynomials
record.statement:
Let $P_n(x)$ denote the polynomials associated with the generalized plane partitions, and let $a$ be an integer with $a\geq 12$. **Turán inequality conjecture.** For every real number $x\geq 1$,

$$
P_a(x)^2>P_{a-1}(x)\,P_{a+1}(x).
$$

This is the polynomial analogue of log-concavity for plane partition numbers and is named a Turán inequality in the source. Numerical zero-distribution evidence verifies the inequality for $12\leq a\leq 100$, while the general assertion remains open.

record.title: Subquadratic upper bound conjecture for the longest solvable board
record.statement: Let $n\geq 3$ be odd, and let $ML(n)$ denote the maximal length of a solvable board of size $n$. The paper establishes the lower bound $ML(n)\geq 3n$ for all $n\geq 11$ and the trivial upper bound $ML(n)\leq n^2$. **Subquadratic upper bound conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$, $ML(n)=o(n^2)$. This is explicitly presented as a weaker conjecture than the linear upper bound conjecture and would still improve the trivial quadratic bound.

record.title: Nesbitt–Shapiro inequality at the remaining endpoint values
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be the number of positive definite matrices in the cyclic sum, and let $F_p$ denote the corresponding cyclic expression. 

**Nesbitt–Shapiro endpoint conjecture.** If $p=12$ or $p=23$, then

$$
F_p\geq \frac{p}{2}n.
$$

The paper explains that this would, together with the preceding proposition and the known cases, establish the inequality for all remaining values in the stated ranges. The parser provides no evidence that these two cases have been resolved, so their status is open.

record.title: da Silva–Sellers congruences for three-colour 3-regular partitions
record.statement:
Let $p_{\{3,3\}}(n)$ denote the number of $3$-regular partitions of $n$ in three colours, with generating function

$$
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}p_{\{3,3\}}(n)q^n=\frac{f_3^3}{f_1^3},
$$

where $f_k=(q^k;q^k)_\infty=\prod_{j=1}^{\infty}(1-q^{jk})$.

**da Silva–Sellers conjecture.** For all $n\geq 0$,

$$
p_{\{3,3\}}(15n+6)\equiv 0\pmod{5},
$$

$$
p_{\{3,3\}}(25n+6)\equiv 0\pmod{5},
$$

$$
p_{\{3,3\}}(25n+16)\equiv 0\pmod{5},
$$

$$
p_{\{3,3\}}(25n+21)\equiv 0\pmod{5}.
$$

These are Ramanujan-like congruences modulo $5$ for the coefficients of the generating function of three-colour $3$-regular partitions. The source presents them as conjectural congruences attributed to da Silva and Sellers; no resolution is stated here.
record.source_name: Ajit Singh and Rupam Barman, “Proof of some conjectural congruences of da Silva and Sellers”, arXiv:2110.14159 (2021).

record.title: Schlosser's quadratic-residue $q$-product conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p$ be prime. For each such $p$, let $a_p$ and $b_p$ range over the quadratic residues and quadratic non-residues modulo $p$, respectively, and define $\omega_p(n)$ by

$$
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\omega_p(n)q^n=\prod_{1\leq a_p,b_p\leq p-1}\dfrac{\left(q^{b_p};q^p\right)_\infty}{\left(q^{a_p};q^p\right)_\infty}.
$$

**Schlosser's conjecture.** For every $n\geq0$, the four families of coefficient identities stated in the source hold for $p=13,17,29,53$, with the displayed residue sets and shifts.

The paper attributes these empirical identities to Schlosser. The supplied text gives no resolution.

record.title: Matching-coefficient conjecture for the $21$-, $28$-, and $77$-modulus products
record.statement:
Define $\omega_{21}(n),\omega_{28}(n),\omega_{77}(n)$ by the three explicit $q$-product generating functions in the source, using $(a;q)_\infty$ for the $q$-Pochhammer symbol. 

**Matching-coefficient conjecture.** For every $n\geq0$, the following identities hold:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega_{21}(21n+r)&=\omega_{21}^{\prime}(21n+r-4),&&r\in\{4,6,10,11,13,17,18,20,24\},\\
\omega_{28}(56n+r)&=\omega_{28}^{\prime}(56n+r-8),&&r\in\{14,21,38\},\\
\omega_{77}(77n+r)&=\omega_{77}^{\prime}(77n+r-24),&&r\in\{27,28,35,37,48,49,65,70,72,76,79,83,90,93,98\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These are empirical conjectures about matching coefficients of further $q$-products and their reciprocals; the supplied text gives no resolution.

record.title: Monotonicity of inversion probability in skew Brownian permutons
record.statement:
Let $\bm \mu_{\rho,q}$ be a skew Brownian permuton with parameters $(\rho,q)\in(-1,1]\times[0,1]$, and define

$$
f(\rho,q)=\mathbb{P}(\operatorname{Perm}_2(\bm \mu_{\rho,q})=21).
$$

Here $21$ is the inversion pattern of size two. **Inversion monotonicity conjecture.** For every fixed $\rho\in(-1,1]$, the function $f(\rho,q)$ is increasing in $q$. An explicit formula for $f(\rho,q)$ is posed as a further problem, and the supplied text does not give a resolution of this monotonicity claim.

record.title: Asymptotic formula for suffix-restricted squares in base 10
record.statement:
For a base $B\ge 2$ and a digit set $D\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,B-1\}$ with $|D|\ge 2$, let $\omega_B^D(n)$ denote the number of $n$-digit suffixes in base $B$ from $D$ that occur as the suffix of a square. **Suffix-count conjecture.** For all $n\ge 3$,

$$
\omega_{10}^{\{7,8,9\}}(n)=8\cdot 3^{n-3}.
$$

This is a computer-supported conjectural pattern for the specified suffix digits; the source gives no proof or resolution.

record.title: Dvořák–Feghali linear diameter conjecture for list recolouring of planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a planar graph on $n$ vertices. A **list assignment** $L$ assigns a set $L(v)$ of colours to each vertex $v\in V$, and let $\mathcal{G}(G,L)$ be the graph whose vertices are the proper $L$-colourings of $G$, with edges between colourings differing on exactly one vertex. **Dvořák–Feghali's conjecture.** If $|L(v)|\geq 10$ for every $v\in V$, then

$$
\mathcal{G}(G,L)\text{ has diameter }O(n).
$$

A linear bound is known for ordinary recolouring of planar graphs with ten colours, but the corresponding list-colouring statement remains the subject of the cited conjecture; the paper addresses it with further results.
record.source_name: Valentin Bartier, Nicolas Bousquet, Carl Feghali, Marc Heinrich, Benjamin Moore and Théo Pierron, “Recolouring planar graphs of girth at least five”, arXiv:2112.00631 (2021).

record.title: New conjecture on balanced-sequence critical exponents
record.statement:
Let a **balanced sequence** over an alphabet of size $d$ be an infinite sequence in which, for any two factors of equal length, the number of occurrences of each letter differs by at most $1$. The **critical exponent** of a sequence is the supremum of the exponents of its nonempty factors, and the minimal critical exponent is the infimum of these values over balanced sequences on the given alphabet.

**New conjecture.** For every alphabet size $d\geq 11$, the minimal critical exponent of a balanced sequence over a $d$-letter alphabet equals

$$
\frac{d-1}{d-2}.
$$

The paper proves the lower bound and constructs sequences attaining it for every even $d\geq 12$. The conjecture therefore remains open for alphabets of odd size.
record.source_name: Lubomíra Dvořáková, Daniela Opočenská, Edita Pelantová and Arseny M. Shur, “On minimal critical exponent of balanced sequences”, arXiv:2112.02854 (2021).

record.title: Weiner's enumeration conjecture for pattern-avoiding Grassmannian permutations
record.statement:
Let $\mathscr{G}_m(12\cdots k)$ denote the set of Grassmannian permutations of size $m$ that avoid the increasing pattern $12\cdots k$, and let $C_r=\frac{1}{r+1}\binom{2r}{r}$ be the $r$th Catalan number. For integers $k\geq 2$ and $m\in\{k,\dots,2k-2\}$, **Weiner's conjecture.**

$$
\left|\mathscr{G}_{m}(12\cdots k)\right|=\sum_{j=1}^{k-\lfloor m/2\rfloor}(-1)^{j-1}j\binom{2k-m-j}{j}C_{k-j}.
$$

The formula generalizes the previously established Catalan-number values at $m=2k-3$ and $m=2k-2$. It was verified by the authors for $k\leq 12$, but a proof for all $k$ and the stated range of $m$ remains open.
record.source_name: Juan B. Gil and Jessica A. Tomasko, “Restricted Grassmannian permutations”, arXiv:2112.03338 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03338

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

record.title: Forster's conjecture on proper holomorphic embeddings of open Riemann surfaces
record.statement: An **open connected Riemann surface** is a connected one-dimensional Stein manifold. **Forster's conjecture.** Every open connected Riemann surface embeds properly holomorphically into $\mathbb{C}^2$. Forster's conjecture is the one-dimensional case of the optimal embedding-dimension problem for Stein manifolds. It was proved by Stensønes and Globevnik in 1995 for every finitely connected planar domain without isolated boundary points, but the supplied context does not state a proof in full generality.
record.source_name: Erlend Fornæss Wold and Giovanni Domenico Di Salvo, “Proper Holomorphic Embeddings of complements of large Cantor sets in C^2”, arXiv:2112.07514 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.07514

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2021).

record.title: The irreducibility conjecture for universal Severi varieties of K3 surfaces
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal F_g$ be the irreducible $19$-dimensional moduli stack of primitively polarized $K3$ surfaces of genus $g$, and let $\mathcal{V}_{g,\delta}$ be the universal Severi variety parametrizing $\delta$-nodal curves on the corresponding polarized surfaces, for $0\leq \delta\leq g$.

**Universal Severi irreducibility conjecture.** For every $0\leq \delta\leq g$, the universal Severi variety $\mathcal{V}_{g,\delta}$ is irreducible.

This is a weaker form of the fiberwise Severi irreducibility conjecture and was considered more approachable. The source presents it as a conjectural statement; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
record.source_name: Andrea Bruno and Margherita Lelli-Chiesa, “Irreducibility of Severi varieties on K3 surfaces”, arXiv:2112.09398 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1611.07423](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.07423).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09398

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

record.title: Classification conjecture for monomially irreducible integers
record.statement:
Let $N\geq 2$. An integer $N$ is **monomially irreducible** if it satisfies the monomial irreducibility property defined in the paper.

**Classification conjecture.** $N$ is monomially irreducible if and only if

$$
N\in\{4,6,8,12,24\}
$$

or $N$ is prime.

The preceding results establish this classification for all monomially irreducible integers below $17440$ and provide necessary conditions for odd integers. A complete classification remains open.
record.source_name: Flavien Mabilat, “Entiers monomialement irréductibles”, arXiv:2112.10410 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10410

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

record.title: Conjecture on singular regularisation parameters for multiple t-values
record.statement:
Let $(\lambda_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}$ be the sequence of singular regularisation parameters, beginning

$$
(\lambda_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}=\left(0,2,\frac{28}{11},\frac{242}{91},\frac{64472}{23479},\ldots\right).
$$

**Conjecture on singular regularisation parameters.** The sequence is increasing and bounded by $3$:

$$
\lambda_{i+1}>\lambda_i,\qquad \lambda_i<3\quad\text{for all }i,
$$

and it converges to $3$:

$$
\lim_{i\to\infty}\lambda_i=3.
$$

These parameters arise from singular regularisations in the motivic multiple $t$-value computations; the source reports numerical and structural evidence but no proof of these three properties.
record.source_name: Steven Charlton, “On motivic multiple t values, Saha's basis conjecture, and generators of alternating MZV's”, arXiv:2112.14613 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.14613

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

record.title: Heim–Neuhauser–Tröger's log-concavity conjecture for the plane partition function
record.statement:
Let $\mathrm{PL}(n)$ denote the number of plane partitions of size $n$. A sequence is **log-concave** if $\mathrm{PL}(n)^2\geq \mathrm{PL}(n-1)\mathrm{PL}(n+1)$ whenever the relevant indices are defined.

**Heim–Neuhauser–Tröger's conjecture.** The function $\mathrm{PL}(n)$ is log-concave for every integer $n\geq 12$.

Heim, Neuhauser, and Tröger proved log-concavity for sufficiently large $n$; the conjecture asserts the explicit threshold $n=12$. The present paper proves this conjecture.
record.source_name: Ken Ono, Sudhir Pujahari and Larry Rolen, “Turán inequalities for the plane partition function”, arXiv:2201.01352 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01352

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Spectral bounds for superspecial abelian-surface isogeny graphs
record.statement:
Let $p\ge 5$ and let $\ell\ne p$ be prime. Let $\mathcal{G}^{SS}_{2}(\ell,p)$ be the superspecial isogeny graph, with normalized adjacency eigenvalues

$$
1=\mu_1>\mu_2\ge\cdots\ge\mu_m>-1,
$$

where $m=|SS_2(p)|$, and set $\lambda_i=1-\mu_i$. Write $N_2(\ell)$ for the graph degree. **Spectral-bound conjecture.** For every $i$,

$$
1-\frac{\max\{4\ell\sqrt{\ell},\ell^2+1+2\ell\sqrt{\ell}\}}{N_2(\ell)}\le \lambda_i\le 1+\frac{4\ell\sqrt{\ell}}{N_2(\ell)}.
$$

In particular, for $\ell=2$,

$$
1-\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{15}=0.24575\ldots\le\lambda_2,\qquad 2-\lambda_m\le 1+\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{15}=1.75425\ldots.
$$

The proposed bounds combine the expected estimate for non-CAP forms with the larger Saito–Kurokawa contribution; the source gives no resolution of this spectral statement.
record.source_name: Yusuke Aikawa, Ryokichi Tanaka and Takuya Yamauchi, “Isogeny graphs on superspecial abelian varieties: Eigenvalues and Connection to Bruhat-Tits buildings”, arXiv:2201.04293 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.04293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: Compatibility-frame representation conjecture for finite lattices
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a nondegenerate finite lattice. A **compatibility frame** is a pair $(X,\vartriangleleft)$, and $\mathfrak{L}(X,\vartriangleleft)$ denotes the lattice represented by that frame.

**Compatibility-frame representation conjecture.** There is a compatibility frame $(X,\vartriangleleft)$ with

$$
|X|<|L|
$$

such that $L$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(X,\vartriangleleft)$.

This gives a finite representation result stronger than merely representing finite lattices: the representing frame has strictly fewer points than the lattice has elements. The supplied text reports verification for every lattice up to size $16$, but does not state a general proof or resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Wesley H. Holliday, “Compatibility and accessibility: lattice representations for semantics of non-classical and modal logics”, arXiv:2201.07098 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.07098

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: The strict P-partition enumerator conjecture for tree posets
record.statement:
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite posets whose Hasse diagrams are trees, and let $\overline{K}_{P}(\mathbf{x})$ denote the strict $P$-partition enumerator. **The strict P-partition enumerator conjecture.** If $P$ and $Q$ are not isomorphic, then

$$
\overline{K}_{P}(\mathbf{x})\neq \overline{K}_{Q}(\mathbf{x}).
$$

The conjecture would imply the chromatic quasisymmetric function conjecture for directed trees, because $\overline{K}_{P}(\mathbf{x})$ is the coefficient of the highest power of $t$ in the chromatic quasisymmetric function associated with a directed acyclic graph. It has been verified for all posets with at most 11 elements and appears as a question in work of Hamaker and Tseng; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Jean-Christophe Aval, Karimatou Djenabou and Peter R. W. McNamara, “Quasisymmetric functions distinguishing trees”, arXiv:2201.11763 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11763

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: The principal specialization conjecture for tree posets
record.statement:
Let $P$ and $Q$ be posets with $n$ elements whose Hasse diagrams are trees. Let $\overline{K}_{P}(\mathbf{x})$ denote the strict $P$-partition enumerator, and specialize $x_i=q^{i-1}$ for $1\leq i\leq n$ and $x_i=0$ thereafter. **The principal specialization conjecture for tree posets.** If $P$ and $Q$ are not isomorphic, then

$$
\overline{K}_{P}(1,q,q^2,\ldots,q^{n-1})\neq \overline{K}_{Q}(1,q,q^2,\ldots,q^{n-1}).
$$

The conjecture has been verified for all posets with at most 10 elements. The source further reports that the shorter specialization through $q^{n-2}$ appears sufficient, but presents that stronger-looking assertion only as an observation rather than a separate conjecture.
record.source_name: Jean-Christophe Aval, Karimatou Djenabou and Peter R. W. McNamara, “Quasisymmetric functions distinguishing trees”, arXiv:2201.11763 (2023).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11763

record.title: Quadratic subword-complexity conjecture for the Thue–Morse two-block fixed point
record.statement:
Let $x^{(00)}$ be the fixed point of the Thue–Morse two-block substitution, and let $p^{(00)}(n)$ denote its subword complexity, namely the number of distinct factors of length $n$. **Quadratic subword-complexity conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
p^{(00)}(n)\geq cn^2
$$

for all $n=1,2,\dots$. The displayed initial values of the complexity function support quadratic growth, but no proof is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Michel Dekking and Mike Keane, “Two-block substitutions and morphic words”, arXiv:2202.13548 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13548

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: Uniform recurrence conjecture for the Thue–Morse two-block fixed point
record.statement: Let $x^{(00)}$ be the fixed point of the Thue–Morse two-block substitution. A word is **uniformly recurrent** when every finite factor occurring in $x^{(00)}$ occurs there with bounded gaps. **Uniform recurrence conjecture.** $x^{(00)}$ is uniformly recurrent. Uniform recurrence is presented as one of the conjectures related to the difficulty of understanding the language of this fixed point, alongside questions about word frequencies.
record.source_name: Michel Dekking and Mike Keane, “Two-block substitutions and morphic words”, arXiv:2202.13548 (2023).

record.title: Odd rational palindrome quotient conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p>1$ be odd. A rational number $p/q$ has a palindromic quotient representation if there are palindromic numbers $A$ and $B$ such that $p/q=A/B$. **Odd rational palindrome quotient conjecture.** For every odd number $p>1$ with $p\ne 23$, there exists an odd number $q<p$ such that $p/q=A/B$ has a solution in palindromes $A,B$.

The conjecture is based on the paper’s automaton construction and computational study of rational solutions; the source does not state a proof or resolution.
record.source_name: James Haoyu Bai, Joseph Meleshko, Samin Riasat and Jeffrey Shallit, “Quotients of Palindromic and Antipalindromic Numbers”, arXiv:2202.13694 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13694

record.title: Rational antipalindromic quotient conjecture
record.statement:
A rational number $p/q$ has an antipalindromic quotient representation if there are antipalindromic numbers $A$ and $B$ such that $p/q=A/B$. **Rational antipalindromic quotient conjecture.** For every integer $p\geq 4$, there exists an integer $q<p$ such that $p/q=A/B$ has a solution in antipalindromes $A,B$.

The conjecture is based on computations for $p>q$ and $p\leq 1000$, following an algorithm that decides whether a given rational number has an antipalindromic quotient representation; the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: James Haoyu Bai, Joseph Meleshko, Samin Riasat and Jeffrey Shallit, “Quotients of Palindromic and Antipalindromic Numbers”, arXiv:2202.13694 (2022).

record.title: The growth conjecture for TP obstructions
record.statement:
A **TP obstruction** is a pattern that is not TP-completable, where TP-completability means that every partial totally positive matrix with the pattern admits a totally positive completion. The number of rows of a pattern is its height.

**TP-obstruction growth conjecture.** There are infinitely many TP obstructions, and the number of TP obstructions with a given number of rows grows quickly, perhaps exponentially, with the number of rows.

The conjecture is motivated by the discovery of 78 new obstructions among the $4$-by-$4$ patterns, a number six times the total number of obstructions for all $3$-by-$n$ patterns. The paper provides no resolution of the asserted infinitude or growth rate.
record.source_name: Daniel Carter and Charles Johnson, “An Atomic Viewpoint of the TP Completion Problem”, arXiv:2203.04484 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.04484

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: The upper-bound conjecture for the general Smarandache sigma product
record.statement:
Let $c(n)$ be the sum of the products of the digits of the first $n$ numbers, and define

$$
h(n)=\frac{25}{44}\Bigl[45^{\log_{10}(n)}-1\Bigr]+\frac{5}{11}\Bigl[45^{\log_{10}(\frac{n+2}{10})+1}-1\Bigr].
$$

**Upper-bound conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{10^k-1:k\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}\}$,

$$
c(n)\leq h(n).
$$

The claim strengthens the preceding upper bound by omitting the additional digit-product term $C(n)$ away from the exceptional values $10^k-1$. The paper presents numerical comparisons suggesting that these are the only exceptions, but provides no proof of the asserted bound.
record.source_name: Luca Onnis, “On the general Smarandache's sigma product of digits”, arXiv:2203.07227 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.07227

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: 2-speciality conjecture for quadratic multiplier polynomials
record.statement: For $m\geq 2$ and $n\geq 1$, let $P_{m,n}$ denote the multiplier polynomial in the quadratic case $d=2$. A polynomial is called **2-special** when it has the special coefficient and divisibility properties defined earlier in the paper. **2-speciality conjecture.** The polynomial $P_{m,n}$ is 2-special. The authors verified this computationally for all pairs $(m,n)$ with $m+n\leq 10$; by the paper's theorem on 2-special polynomials, it would imply the multiplier-resultant conjecture for $d=2$.
record.source_name: Robert L. Benedetto and Vefa Goksel, “Misiurewicz polynomials and dynamical units, Part II”, arXiv:2203.14431 (2022).

record.title: Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp unbalanced sparse-subset conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph and let $alpha$ be an arbitrary constant with $53/120\leq \alpha\leq 1$. Let $\beta$ satisfy

$$
\beta>\begin{cases} (2\alpha-1)/4, & \text{when } 17/30\leq \alpha\leq 1, \\ (5\alpha-2)/25 & \text{when } 53/120\leq \alpha\leq 17/30. \end{cases}
$$
 If $n$ is sufficiently large and every $\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor$-subset of $V(G)$ spans at least $\beta n^2$ edges, then $G$ contains a triangle. **Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp's conjecture.** The stated implication holds. The conjecture is known for $\alpha\geq0.6$ and was disproved for $\alpha<0.474$, so the source records it as a conjectural statement over the displayed range rather than as a universally settled result.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Felix Christian Clemen and Bernard Lidický, “10 Problems for Partitions of Triangle-free Graphs”, arXiv:2203.15764 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15764

record.title: Rudin–Shapiro arithmetic-progression bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{r}$ denote the Rudin–Shapiro sequence, and let $A_{\mathbf{r}}(d)$ be its associated arithmetic-progression counting function.

**Rudin–Shapiro bound conjecture.** For all $d \geq 23$,

$$
A_{\mathbf{r}}(d) \leq \frac{1}{2}(d+7).
$$

Moreover, equality holds if and only if $d=2^k-1$ for some odd $k \geq 5$.
The conjecture is intended to provide a sharp linear bound and, together with a stated theorem, would imply the subsequent estimates for maxima over $d<2^k$.
record.source_name: Bartosz Sobolewski, “On monochromatic arithmetic progressions in binary words associated with pattern sequences”, arXiv:2204.05287 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.05287

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: The punctured-disk zero-free conjecture for series-parallel graphs
record.statement:
Let $B_{5/27}(1)$ denote the disk of radius $5/27$ centered at $1$, and let $Z(G;q)$ be the chromatic polynomial of a series-parallel graph $G$. **The punctured-disk zero-free conjecture.** For every

$$
q\in B_{5/27}(1)\setminus\{1\}
$$

and every series-parallel graph $G$, one has

$$
Z(G;q)\neq 0.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the paper's computational picture and the preceding zero-free criterion. No proof or disproof is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Ferenc Bencs, Jeroen Huijben and Guus Regts, “On the location of chromatic zeros of series-parallel graphs”, arXiv:2204.10038 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.10038

record.title: Existence of non-central idempotents in simple Lie algebras of characteristic 2
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra over a field of characteristic $2$. An **idempotent** is an element $l\in L$ such that

$$
(ad_L(l))^2=ad_L(l).
$$

A \mathbb{Z}_2-grading of $L$ is **non-degenerate** when its nonzero homogeneous components are both nonzero; an idempotent is non-central when it is not in the center of $L$.

**Non-central idempotent conjecture.** Every finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra over a field of characteristic $2$ has a non-central idempotent, and hence a non-degenerate $\mathbb{Z}_2$-grading.

The conjecture is motivated by computations of idempotents and their $\operatorname{Aut}(L)$-orbits in known simple Lie algebras of dimension at most $20$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Its status is not established in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Bettina Eick and Tobias Moede, “Computing subalgebras and Z_2-gradings of simple Lie algebras over finite fields”, arXiv:2205.03155 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03155

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Bostan's conjecture on Catalan numbers modulo 10
record.statement:
Let $C(n)$ denote the $n$th Catalan number. The conjecture concerns which residue classes modulo $10$ are attained by these numbers.

**Bostan's conjecture.** The following assertions hold:

1. For all $n\geq 0$, $C(n)\mathrel{\not\equiv}3\pmod{10}$.
2. For sufficiently large $n$, $C(n)\mathrel{\not\equiv}1,7,9\pmod{10}$.

This conjecture was observed by Alin Bostan in 2015 and later popularized in 2018. The supplied source presents it as unresolved, in the context of the difficulty of proving analogous residue-avoidance results for non-prime-power moduli.
record.source_name: Armin Straub, “On congruence schemes for constant terms and their applications”, arXiv:2205.09902 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.09902

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2022). “As an application, we consider an open question of Rowland and Yassawi that asks whether there exist infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p^2$ never divides any Motzkin number $M (n)$.”
